sections.title: Tree and habitat
sections.text: Taxodium distichum, the bald cypress, is a deciduous conifer of the southeastern United States, often growing on wet or seasonally flooded ground. It can reach about 30–46 m in height; mature landscape trees commonly spread 7.6–10.7 m. Its feathery, two-ranked leaves turn brown and fall in autumn, as shown in the plate.

sections.title: Cones and knees
sections.text: The globose woody seed cones measure about 1.3–3.6 cm across and turn from green to brownish purple. In swampy sites, roots can form upright woody projections called knees, from a few centimetres to more than 3.7 m high. These characteristic knees are shown around the illustrated trunk.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The sources consulted document timber use but not a reliable human food use or species-specific toxicity profile.
